misconception: Every chat starts from nothing — Claude can never remember or persist anything.

mentorLessons.line: A Project is a self-contained workspace — its own chats, its own knowledge base — one home for everything a piece of work needs.
Set project instructions once and every chat inside that Project follows them — tone, role, rules — no repeating yourself.
Anything shelved in a Project's knowledge base serves every chat inside it — but chats don't read each other; only the shelf is shared.
Claude quietly distills your chat history into a synthesis of key insights — who you are, what you're working on — and carries it into new conversations.
Memory is yours to govern — view it, edit it, pause it, or reset it entirely from your settings.
An incognito chat leaves no trace — it is saved neither to memory nor to your chat history.
Each Project keeps its own separate memory space, so what Claude learns in one Project never bleeds into another.
When content is substantial and standalone — a document, code, a diagram, an interactive page — Claude sets it in its own dedicated window: an artifact.
Artifacts keep versions you can flip between, can be downloaded, and can be published so anyone with the link may use them — but once unpublished, that same artifact can't be published again.
Instructions shape how Claude behaves, knowledge is what it consults, memory is what it recalls about you, and artifacts are what it builds for you.

questions.prompt: You're starting a months-long redesign with lots of recurring context. What's the right container for the work?
choices: One very long chat you never close
A new chat each day, re-pasting the context
A Project — a workspace with its own chats and knowledge base
Nothing — context can never persist between chats
questions.reteach: A Project is a self-contained workspace whose chats and knowledge base stay together across the whole effort.
hardChoices: Claude's memory — it stores full context so no workspace is needed
A single artifact that every future chat automatically reads
Custom instructions in settings — they hold project context globally

questions.prompt: What actually lives inside a Project?
choices: Its own chat history plus a shared knowledge base
Only a single pinned chat
Just bookmarks pointing to chats elsewhere
Nothing persistent — Projects are purely cosmetic folders
questions.reteach: A Project holds its own chats and its own knowledge base — a genuine workspace, not a label.
hardChoices: A single continuous chat that all project work shares
Chats that automatically read each other's full context
A knowledge base only — chats stay outside the Project

questions.prompt: You want Claude to always answer as a cautious legal reviewer in every chat about one contract job. Best move?
choices: Retype the role at the start of every chat
Set project instructions — they apply to all chats in that Project
Say it in one chat and trust the others to notice
Rename the Project to 'cautious legal reviewer'
questions.reteach: Project instructions are applied to every chat inside that Project, so a role or tone only needs stating once.
hardChoices: Ask Claude to memorize the role — memory applies it to every chat
Upload the role as a document to the project knowledge base
State it once in any Project chat — the others share its context

choices: Only the first chat created after you save them
Every chat in every Project you own
Nothing unless memory is also switched on
Every chat inside that one Project
questions.reteach: Project instructions are scoped to their own Project — all its chats, and only its chats.
hardChoices: Every chat in that Project plus any chats you start outside it
Only new chats created after saving — earlier chats never see them
Every chat, but only while a copy sits in the knowledge base

questions.prompt: You upload a style guide to a Project's knowledge base. Which chats can use it?
choices: Only the chat that was open during the upload
All chats within that Project
Every chat everywhere, even outside the Project
None, until you also paste it into each chat
questions.reteach: Anything uploaded to a Project's knowledge base is used across all of the chats within that Project.
hardChoices: Only chats created after the upload, not earlier ones
Any chat, once memory has summarized the guide into your profile
All chats in that Project, but only if instructions cite the file

questions.prompt: Where should reference documents go so Claude can consult them in every chat of a Project?
choices: Pasted into every new chat by hand
Into Claude's memory, by asking it to memorize them verbatim
Uploaded to the Project's knowledge base
Into the Project's title and description
questions.reteach: The knowledge base is the Project's shelf — upload documents there and every chat in the Project can draw on them.
hardChoices: Pasted into the project instructions as full document text
Attached to one chat — Project chats share uploads automatically
Saved as an artifact so every chat can reference it

questions.prompt: In Chat A inside a Project you worked out a naming scheme. Will Chat B in the same Project automatically know it?
choices: Yes — all chats in a Project share full context automatically
Only if Chat B was created after Chat A
No — chats don't share context unless the information is added to the project knowledge base
No, and there is no way to share it at all
questions.reteach: Chats in a Project stay separate — to share something between them, add it to the project knowledge base.
hardChoices: Yes — project memory syncs decisions between chats in real time
Yes — the knowledge base captures chat decisions automatically
No — and Project memory can't carry anything between chats either

questions.prompt: How does Claude's memory get its content?
choices: Claude automatically summarizes your conversations into a synthesis of key insights
You must type every memory in by hand
It scans the files on your device
It can't — every chat starts from absolute nothing
questions.reteach: Memory builds itself: Claude summarizes your chat history into key insights that inform new conversations.
hardChoices: It stores full transcripts of every past conversation
It pulls from documents uploaded to your Projects' knowledge bases
It only saves details you explicitly tell Claude to remember

questions.prompt: What kind of things does Claude's memory tend to hold?
choices: Verbatim transcripts of every chat you've ever had
Your account password and payment details
Only what was said within the current conversation
Your role, projects, preferences, and working style — work-focused context
questions.reteach: Memory is a work-focused synthesis — role, projects, and preferences — not a verbatim transcript archive.
hardChoices: A condensed but complete log of each chat, kept chat-by-chat
Everything in your Projects' knowledge bases, synced automatically
Only preferences you explicitly asked Claude to remember

questions.prompt: Claude's memory holds something about your workflow that's now outdated. What can you do?
choices: Nothing — memory is permanent and read-only
View and edit the memory in settings, or ask Claude to update it
Delete your whole account — it's the only way
Wait for the memory to expire on its own
questions.reteach: You can view and edit everything Claude remembers about you in settings, or simply ask Claude to change it.
hardChoices: Export memory, edit the file, and re-import — the only way to change it
Manage it from inside an incognito chat, where memory is edited
Reset memory entirely — individual details can't be changed

questions.prompt: You want Claude to keep what it already knows about you but stop adding anything new. Which control fits?
choices: Pause memory — existing memories stay, but no new ones are added
Reset memory — pausing and resetting are the same thing
Start an incognito chat — that permanently changes memory settings
No such control exists
questions.reteach: Pausing memory freezes it — existing memories remain usable while nothing new is recorded; reset is the separate, permanent wipe.
hardChoices: Pause memory — but paused memories are hidden until you resume
Use incognito for every chat — it keeps old memories applying
Edit the memory summary and add a note telling Claude to stop

questions.prompt: You need a one-off conversation that leaves no trace in memory or chat history. What do you use?
choices: A regular chat — just delete one message afterwards
A brand-new Project with no documents
An incognito chat
Impossible — everything is always remembered forever
questions.reteach: Incognito chats are saved neither to Claude's memory nor to your chat history — a genuinely traceless conversation.
hardChoices: A chat with memory paused — pausing also hides it from history
A new Project — its separate memory keeps the chat out of history
Any chat you delete afterward — deletion also wipes it from memory

questions.prompt: You use one Project for marketing and another for engineering. How does memory treat them?
choices: One global memory blends everything from both
Each project has its own separate memory space and summary
Only the first-created Project gets any memory
Using Projects disables memory entirely
questions.reteach: Each Project has its own separate memory space, keeping context focused and isolated from other Projects.
hardChoices: Projects share one memory, but instructions keep contexts apart
Each Project gets separate memory only if you enable it per Project
Memory stays separate at first but merges into one profile over time

questions.prompt: You ask Claude to build an interactive quiz page. Where does substantial, standalone content like this appear?
choices: Buried inline in the chat text only
Sent to you as an email attachment
In an artifact — a dedicated window separate from the main conversation
Nowhere — Claude can't produce interactive content
questions.reteach: Substantial, standalone content becomes an artifact: a dedicated window beside the conversation that you can iterate on and reuse.
hardChoices: In the Project knowledge base, where interactive files are stored
As a download only — interactive content can't render inside Claude
Published to a share link first — that's the only way it can run

questions.prompt: Which of these would typically be an artifact?
choices: A single-page HTML site, an SVG diagram, or an interactive React component
A one-line answer to a quick factual question
Claude's private reasoning before it replies
Your memory summary from settings
questions.reteach: Artifacts carry substantial standalone work — documents, code, HTML pages, SVGs, diagrams, React components — not quick inline replies.
hardChoices: Project instructions, since they're substantial standalone text
Any document you upload to a Project's knowledge base
A Project's chat history, packaged for download

questions.prompt: You've iterated an artifact five times and now prefer the second version. Can you get it back?
choices: No — each edit permanently destroys the previous version
Only by re-prompting the whole thing from scratch
Only if you had copied it out beforehand
Yes — use the version selector to switch between versions
questions.reteach: Artifacts keep their versions — the version selector lets you switch back to any earlier one.
hardChoices: Yes — but only if the artifact was published before the edits
Yes — restore it from the Project's knowledge base backup
Only within the same session — versions vanish when the chat closes

questions.prompt: You publish an artifact. Who can open it?
choices: Only you, ever
Anyone with the link — even people without a Claude account can view and interact
Only members of the same Project
Publishing just saves a private backup copy
questions.reteach: Publishing makes an artifact publicly available — anyone with the link can view and interact with it, no account required.
hardChoices: Anyone with the link, but they must sign in to a Claude account
Anyone with the link can view it, but only you can interact
Anyone in your organization, but no one outside it

questions.prompt: You want three things: Claude always uses your brand voice in one Project's chats, a brand PDF stays available there, and you get an editable one-page site. Match the tools, in order.
choices: Project instructions, project knowledge base, artifact
Memory, artifact, incognito chat
Artifact, memory, project instructions
One long chat covers all three
questions.reteach: Instructions govern behavior in a Project, the knowledge base holds its documents, and artifacts are the standalone things Claude builds.
hardChoices: Project instructions, memory, artifact
Memory, project knowledge base, artifact
Project knowledge base, project instructions, artifact
